Doors
DORZ
proper noun (Gen Alpha slang)
Doors (styled DOORS), a Roblox horror game released in August 2022 by the studio LSPLASH. Players move through a hotel of a hundred numbered doors, hiding in closets from monsters called Rush, Ambush, Seek, Screech, Halt, and Figure; later floors (The Mines, 2024) extended the game. It became one of the most popular horror games on Roblox, and its monster names and jump-scares became Gen Alpha playground lore — "Rush is coming, hide!"

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

Doors is a Roblox horror game: you walk through a scary hotel, door after door, and hide when monsters come. Gen Alpha kids love the jump-scares and act them out at recess, and many younger siblings watch over a shoulder and have nightmares. The Christian observation: the game’s very title is a word Jesus took for Himself. "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture" (Joh 10:9). Behind the game’s doors is something to fear; behind Christ’s door is safety and pasture. He also stands at the door of our hearts: "Behold, I stand at the door, and knock" (Rev 3:20). Scripture does not tell children that nothing is frightening; it tells them who is stronger. "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me" (Psa 23:4), and "God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind" (2Ti 1:7). A father can tell a five-year-old: "That game has scary doors. But Jesus says He is the Door, and when we’re with Him we’re safe. Let’s ask Him for brave hearts." And a father may simply decide the game waits until the child is older — a wise gatekeeper is also a door.

Webster 1828 Definition

Roblox horror game (2022) of a hundred hotel doors and hiding from monsters — fear as entertainment, answered by the One who said "I am the door."

DOORS, proper n. (Roblox horror game, 2022–present; Gen Alpha usage) The hotel-of-a-hundred-doors survival game. "I got to door 100 in Doors!"

Monster names in playground lore: Rush, Ambush, Seek, Figure, Screech, Halt.

Decode for parents: genuinely frightening jump-scare design; younger siblings who watch are the ones most often scared.

Webster 1828, the root — DOOR, n. An opening or passage into a house, or other building, or into any room, apartment or closet, by which persons enter.

Key Scripture

Joh 10:9 — "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture."

Rev 3:20 — "Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me."

Psa 23:4 — "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me."

2Ti 1:7 — "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind."

Modern Corruption

Doors sells the thrill of what waits behind the next door; Scripture names the Door behind which there is no monster, only pasture.

expand to see more

Horror for children works by rehearsing fear without danger, and some children enjoy it while others carry it to bed for weeks. The game’s design is built around dread: the light flickers, the sound warns, you hide and wait. A father must know his own child; what is a thrill to a ten-year-old can be a torment to a five-year-old watching over his shoulder.

Whatever the household decides, give the child the better word. Jesus is the Door; the Good Shepherd keeps the sheep; and perfect love casts out fear. Pray with a frightened child by name, read Psalm 23 aloud, and teach her that the scariest door in the world — death itself — has been opened from the other side by the risen Lord.
